kids.content: “the crux of architecture is not the sculptural pattern, but instead the
building interiors. These can be seen as “negative solids,” as voids
which the artist divides, combines, repeats and emphasizes in the same way as the sculptor treats his “positive” lumps of substance.”
- The “personal styles” of architects are not necessarily based on laws of nature
or on logical reasoning. More important is that they exhibit a
coherent application of an idea which also must be clear that the public can find it out. An advantage is also if the style includes symbolical undertones.
